columns_note: signal_* = picks only, independent of stake size; staking_* = money only, under a named stake plan; gates_* = the validation gates; demotion = the gate that sends a live strategy back to paper

rule.ranking: signal z first, ROI second. A strategy with a positive ROI and a negative z is ranked below a strategy with a better z and a worse ROI, because the ROI of a losing signal is a staking artefact.
rule.staking_independence: every strategy is re-priced under a 5%-of-bankroll compounding plan; a profit that survives only the flat plan is labelled as such
rule.demotion: D-01..D-04, evaluated on every build; any one firing sends the strategy to paper

summary.finding: 1 strategies show a positive ROI but none has a signal that clears the 1.96 z bar. On its own, that ROI would have topped a naive leaderboard. This is exactly the failure mode the split exists to catch: the money was a staking run, not a signal.

defects_found_in_this_build.was: every strategy was tested against a flat 52.38% break-even
defects_found_in_this_build.effect: the two-leg parlay's 30.4% hit rate was scored z = -7.2 although it is 3 points ABOVE its own 27.44% bar; the moneyline's 34.7% was scored z = -19.4 against a bar that applies to no moneyline ticket
defects_found_in_this_build.fixed_in: Poisson-binomial test: each ticket carries its own break-even, the sum of those bars is the expectation, and the z is computed against the sum of the per-ticket variances
defects_found_in_this_build.caught_by: reading the row: a z of -7 with a hit rate near break-even is not a losing strategy, it is a wrong test

defects_found_in_this_build.was: parlay wins were paid at single-leg -110 odds
defects_found_in_this_build.effect: published ROI -40.7% for a strategy that is actually +10.5%
defects_found_in_this_build.caught_by: the same row, after B-01 was fixed: a hit rate above its own bar cannot produce a -40% ROI

defects_found_in_this_build.was: the leaderboard ranked on ROI alone in an early draft
defects_found_in_this_build.effect: the parlay, with the weakest signal on the board (z = 1.00), ranked first
defects_found_in_this_build.fixed_in: rank = (signal z desc, ROI desc); the ROI is shown but never ranks

defects_found_in_this_build.was: a parlay was bucketed 'competitive' only if EVERY leg was a competitive margin, and other strategies were bucketed on their single game's margin
defects_found_in_this_build.effect: one bounce in one leg decides the ticket, so 195 of 234 parlay tickets landed in 'other' and the luck decomposition had n = 39, too small to decompose anything
defects_found_in_this_build.fixed_in: a parlay is variance-dominated if ANY leg is; a decomposition with fewer than 10 tickets is published as 'too few' rather than computed

rows.name: Two-leg side parlay
rows.hypothesis: The two biggest disagreements on a card are independent enough that the parlay's true probability beats the product the book charges for.
rows.falsifier: Realised parlay hit rate is not above the compounded break-even (52.38%^2 = 27.44%) after correlation adjustment.
